Doris "Dorie" Miller was an African American cook in the United States Navy during World War II. He is notable for being one of the first American heroes of World War II.

Here are the key details about Doris K. Miller:

- Doris Miller was born on October 12, 1919 in Waco, Texas. He was the son of Henrietta and Connery Miller, sharecroppers.

- Miller enlisted in the U.S. Navy in 1939 and was assigned as a mess attendant, one of the few roles open to African Americans at the time.

- On December 7, 1941, during the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, Miller manned an anti-aircraft machine gun on the USS West Virginia, even though he had not been trained to use it. He successfully shot down several Japanese aircraft.

- Miller's actions during the Pearl Harbor attack were recognized as heroic. He was awarded the Navy Cross, the second-highest decoration for valor in the U.S. Navy, for his bravery.

- Miller was the first African American to be awarded the Navy Cross. His actions helped challenge the Navy's racial segregation policies and paved the way for greater opportunities for African Americans.

- After Pearl Harbor, Miller went on to serve on other ships in the Pacific theater. He was killed in action on November 24, 1943 when the ship he was on, the USS Liscome Bay, was torpedoed and sunk by a Japanese submarine.

- Doris Miller has been honored with numerous monuments and memorials for his heroism at Pearl Harbor. He is considered an iconic figure in African American history and the civil rights movement.
